item.title: The Two Sides of Queen Elizabeth Have Been Captured in $5,000 Enamels
item.description: The arrival of Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, Charles Spencer’s memoir of his late sibling, has engulfed British tabloids and the global celebrity press. item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: Trump's Casual Threat of Annihilating Iran Ramps Up a Genuine Danger
item.description: Visiting mixed villages in former Yugoslavia before it careened toward its violent breakup in 1992, I spoke to neighbors who dismissed the idea of a coming war as simply unimaginable. But as each tuned in to the increasingly nationalistic TV stations of their respective Serbian or Croatian capitals, they were bombarded by commentary posing as news that recalled historical wrongs and alleged plots for coming atrocities. Steeped in these bilious alternative realties, the neighbors stopped talking.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Hermes has options for addressing its Birkin bag crisis
item.description: It must have been hurtful for the house of Hermes when Emily Oberg, founder of cult label Sporty & Rich, which styles its streetwear with gold Cartier watches and 1980s Porsches, declared that carrying a regular leather Birkin was akin to toting a Coach bag.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.title: Putin’s Shadow War Is Testing NATO’s Restraint
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin, frustrated by his bogged-down war in Ukraine, is trying to intimidate the European nations that — given President Donald Trump’s severe cuts in aid to Kyiv — are now Ukrainians’ main military, economic and diplomatic supporters.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: Iced Coffee at a Job Interview? How About a Seafood Boil?
item.description: How you take your caffeinated beverage is not really a proper question in the corporate world.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Vietnam Can’t Beat China With the Lights Out
item.description: The world’s attempts to reduce its reliance on China’s juggernaut manufacturing sector depend to an outsized extent on just one country: Vietnam. The nation’s efforts to meet those expectations, in turn, may come down to the fate of a handful of mothballed wind farms. With energy costs soaring, the government is warning of blackouts looming as soon as next year. A fix is long overdue.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Morgan Stanley Leaked Some Deals
item.description: Pipelines, force majeure, private equity malaise, credit card risk tranching, egg futures, and Medicaid gambling.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: Go Slow Is the Right Route for China’s Auto Glut
item.description: When it comes to consolidating China’s overcrowded auto industry, bigger isn’t necessarily better. A modest-looking deal involving two state-owned carmakers offers a pragmatic way to start tackling the glut.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: Iced Coffee at Job Interviews Reveals Deeper Workplace Power Struggles
item.description: Is it acceptable to bring an iced coffee to a job interview?
item.dc:creator: Beth Kowitt

item.title: Zuckerberg’s AI Muse Charm Could Be Meta’s iPod Moment
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg is on to something. Hot on the heels of Meta Platforms Inc.’s hugely well-received launch of its Muse personal AI agent, Zuckerberg announced on Wednesday evening the next phase: a “Tamagotchi-like” pendant for interacting with the cuddly assistant on the go. It’s slated to be out in time for Christmas.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: Don't Blame California AG Rob Bonta for Folding on Paramount
item.description: The more details that emerge about the agreement to settle an antitrust lawsuit that would’ve blocked Paramount Skydance’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, the more blame has been heaped on one man: California Attorney General Rob Bonta.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: The White House Press Ban Shows How Tricky Free Speech Can Be
item.description: President Donald Trump’s bid to exclude CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House press pool violates the First Amendment under existing precedent. And on Thursday, a judge temporarily blocked Trump’s ban. But that’s not the end of the story. A close look at the arguments made by the Department of Justice for the hearing that took place Wednesday in federal district court demonstrates just how much press freedom rests on norms and customs, not just the letter of the Constitution.
item.dc:creator: Noah Feldman

item.title: Your 3% Mortgage Rate Is Crippling the Housing Market
item.description: The US housing market has been stuck in neutral for nearly four years, with sales of new and existing homes plodding along at a historically slow pace. One explanation is that the average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage in the US passed 6% four years ago and has stayed above that ever since, creeping past 7% this week.
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: Rich Investors Fleeing Private Credit Pile Into Infrastructure Finance
item.description: The rush for the exits by wealthy investors in private credit funds is far from done. But even as the rich run away from direct lending, they aren’t abandoning alternative assets. Instead, they look to be chasing the next hot thing: infrastructure finance.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Republicans Are Ghosting Trump. It’s Too Late
item.description: When Miami Representative Maria Elvira Salazar stood in front of the White House and recorded her first campaign ad, she told President Donald Trump he had gone “too far on immigration enforcement” and warned that Hispanics who had elected him to office had been betrayed. The loyal Republican’s straight-to-camera critique of Trump immediately became national news.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: The AI Industry Doesn't Seem to Understand Intelligence
item.description: Just three years after OpenAI said its models were good at grade-school math, the company announced they had solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem in 88 hours, something that had stumped humanity’s greatest mathematical minds since the 1930s. Project that trend forward and you see why OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman thinks AI will cure all diseases - and why people are afraid that a rogue AI might harm humanity.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Mukunda
